reviews.text: Update after full release ---------------------------- A wonderful survivor to play with a good playtime if you are a completionist. The weapon variety lets you enjoy the game in various ways and allows for some theory crafting and different strategies to try. The serenity mode gives a fun refreshing way to play and opens to higher levels of challenge and you'll have plenty of time to try and complete challenge 60 with all cats. Still enjoying my time playing after 80+ hours. Still mostly on steam deck. And I think I'll squeeze some more for a full completion! Initial review ---------------------------- A lovely survivor to play on Steam Deck with a good sense of progression run after run. You'll set your own challenge level after the first succesful run and the game will give you plenty of fun time. You already have a good amount of content during the early access, even more promising for the full release.

I don't know how to really "feel" about this game and honestly, I wish steam had a "meh" or a "its mid" button. The "progression" that top reviewers praise about this game is actually slow and boring. Having to beat the easy mode as three different cats to get to bargain mode feels like an immediate grind wall only an hour or so in. Easy mode just feels too "easy" even for casual players like myself that suck at holocure. And then bargain mode is a pretty big wall and requires you to grind in easy mode because bargin mode has no coins to reward you for doing this much harder mode. Bargain mode should be unlocked after beating easy mode once, and you should be rewarded with coins as you grind your way through bargain mode to get to challenge mode. The story is pretty "meh." I thought that as you progress through the game, you would unlock more stages of grief and get to the bottom of this mystery. Maybe its an early access thing and more of the plot will be added later on? I'm not quite sure. The art, while creative and somewhat emotional don't really tell you a story. I think its a really cool idea that the dev put their cat in the game as one last adventure, but I don't really understand what that has to do with the game. As it stands right now, a three stage adventure feels way too short. And another thing I dislike about the game is how little EXP you get from enemies. It feels like you level up extremely slow even with the more experience upgrade. So you quickly get overwhelmed at the start by enemies because you just can't upgrade your weapons fast enough. Then when you get through this annoying wall that is level 1, you get to two and you start to upgrade your weapons and it quickly goes from hard to literally just stand in one spot and win. Also there are pretty much next to zero hearts on the map at a time. To basically artificially inflate the difficulty instead of just making the game harder. It's the same reason why you gain EXP at such a slow rate. The dev knows they made a game way too easy and couldn't come up with a fair and challenging way to spice it up. Even if you have the upgrade that makes more hearts appear and the double hearts, you are not going to be healing much and basically just play the game hitless until the final boss or you lose. Fun. If your lucky, maybe you'll get a family bonus that will help you. Also not having items in this game..........was certainly an interesting choice to change up and simplify the formula of survivor-likes. But this game proves that you should have items, something that gives me more EXP or increases my magnet range. I get that you are supposed to be getting these bonuses from weapon families, but it takes at least five levels to get a family bonus. Which brings me to my next point, there aren't enough weapons in this game to spice up the gameplay. I can count all the weapons on one hand, there's a reason why survivor-likes tend to have a lot of weapons to use, it mixes up the gameplay. Overall, I mean it's worth playing if your bored and have nothing better to do with your time. But really, just play a different survivor-like. 100 percent positive on this game breaks my mind when games like death must die exist. Or other games in the same 3-5 dollar range. Why buy this when you can get much better value for the same price? I mean sure, it'd make a wonderful mobile game for the really baby casual moms and dads but I find it to just be a little boring and repetitive. At least the challenge mode spices things up, but men the path to unlock it just takes too long.

A really interesting mix of emotions about this game. First of all, this is a great entry point to gaming for children and even elderly - however, the theme is surprisingly hard. Kitty's last adventure is about the loss of a pet, and the developer made the game as sort of... channeling that grief into something positive and creative, and I applaud any man on this Earth who can do that. He (she?) reached out to me in difficult times with a free key, and the least I can do is leave a fair review about the game - which is a DEFINITIVE YES, RECOMMENDED. NOTE: The game offers to simply hide the sad cutscenes (more like a simplistic image), if you want to avoid the theme of loss and sadness. You can do this on first start of the game, or anytime in options - this is appriciated if a parent buys this for a kid for the cute looks and easy controls, but doesn't want to drop a nuclear warhead on little Timmy's emotions. For any parent who wants to prepare and teach their children about pets not living forever. For any teen or older who lost a pet. For any gamer who wants to find a cute and friendly introduction to the bullet-heaven roguelite genre created by Vampire Survivors. It is very wife compatible. Despite it's simple looks, it has surprising depth and content to explore which makes it worth replaying over and over. A little bit of constructive criticism: it's often difficult to tell the difference between a pickup, an enemy, and my own weapons due to the white paper frame around everything, but I also must add getting scared by almost bumping into my own poop of titanic proportions is a surprisingly authentic cat experience. If any of the above speaks to you, or you are a grown ass man with a cool beard going through hard times, pick up your leather jacket, put on your sunglasses, and sit down in your couch instead of your nonexistent chopperbike and play this for about an hour. You can thank me later.

Fun fact: My kitten's name is also Kitty! I have 10 hours in this game already and I can say I'm enjoying it a lot. It makes me feel better with myself for some reason. I always smile while playing it and I want to say thanks for creating this cozy experience. I found the game like 1 year ago in my Opera GX browser where there was a demo available and I loved it since the first moment. There was something about it and the story behind the game that made me feel an instant special connection, and I'm very proud to say I even bought the Supporter Pack because I sincerely think the developer deserves it and also to express somwhow my gratitude. I hope that you, the person behind this game, could read this review and I would like to make you smile even a little as I do when I'm playing this game, Kitty's Last Adventure. Thanks again! I promise I will complete every achievement I have left, this game totally deserves it! Kitty will have the best adventure ever!

simple but lovely game! it's kind of like vampire survivors but cats! not as complex, but that's fine! the cats are cute. the gameplay loop is addicting. the mechanics are interesting and I like the family bonuses and weapon types. (stick is my mvp) I've almost 100% it. runs perfect on deck. my only complaints would be 2 main points 1: I'm not sure if it's supposed to take this long, but I only unlocked shadow just now when I'd nearly finished everything. I guess I felt like It was kind of less exciting that way. 2: the stages do get repetitive, as you have to do the same runs with each cat for all achievements. I would love a dlc with extra stages, or an endless mode, or more challenges to mix it up. even just a couple more songs or a color pallete swap for each stage would be nice. but overall I am very happy and felt it was well worth the purchase!!

I received this game for free through Keymailer when it initially released. The dev has been super good about updating the game. I believe it is finally finished, which is why I finally went back and 100%ed it. Kitty's Last Adventure is a cute little vampire survivors style game. It stands out because it has great theming. All the characters are cats with different weapons, all the weapons are cat toys/items, and all the enemies/bosses are things that cats are typically afraid of. There is a little bit of a story that you get in between the three levels, but it is not not very in depth. The story is more shown rather than told. There are 20 different cats to play as, multiple weapons with different paths, there is no weapon combination though, there are three main levels, there is a challenge mode to increase difficulty, and there are two other modes you can play through.
